newsitem.title: UK: Amersham sees growth beating stg strength.
newsitem.headline: Amersham sees growth beating stg strength.

text.p: Amersham International Plc said on Tuesday that although the recent strength of sterling would continue to hit its profits, it expected underlying growth to more than overcome this.

The British health sciences group said it was confident that in the coming years its sales and profit growth would maintain the underlying momentum achieved in 1996/97, before the effect of exchange rates.

"1996/97 has been a year of real achievement, and for the first time there is a balance of earnings between our principal businesses, which are both positioned for growth," said chief executive Bill Castell in the results statement.

Amersham, which has been in talks with Swedish-U.S. group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc about merging their life sciences arms, earlier raised year pretax profits by an expected 30 percent to 65.8 million stg.

The profit included 2.7 million stg of losses because of movements on exchange rates and the loss on sale of Puridec, a part of its industrial quality and safety assurance business, of 1.5 million stg.

Amersham, which lifted its total dividend 22 percent to 22p, said profits in its healthcare business surged 103 percent to 34.9 million stg, boosted by the strenth of its prostrate cancer therapy and heart imaging products.
Margins rose to 16 percent from 12 percent.
In its life science operations, profits rose eight percent to 37.4 million stg on overall sales of 174 million stg -- a four percent rise. Margins rose one percent to 23 percent, the group said.
